analysis.title: Liquid Insight: Bank of Canada preview: hawkish hold vs largely priced hike
key_insights: BofA expects the Bank of Canada to hold at 2.25% on Oct 28, but calls it a close call. Weak activity and core inflation below target favor a pause, while inflation expectations and hawkish BoC communication leave meaningful hike risk.

Either outcome is expected to come with hawkish communication and a move higher in December hike pricing. A hike would be seen as the start of a small adjustment (2 total hikes), not a full hiking cycle.
September employment fell 68.3k, the second consecutive monthly decline, taking cumulative 2026 job creation to -41.2k. Unemployment rose to 6.5% and wage growth was 2.3% yoy.
Headline inflation rose to 3.1% yoy on higher gasoline prices, while the average of the BoC's core measures (CPI-trimmed and CPI-median) fell to 1.9%, below the 2% target.

The Consumer Expectations Survey shows longer-term inflation expectations rising to match elevated shorter-term expectations. This could make the BoC less willing to look through the current supply shock. Market-based inflation expectations are also trending up.
Trade uncertainty remains elevated, with no US-Canada trade deal expected before the US midterm elections. BofA sees this as a counterweight to the case for tightening.

The BoC will use a new forecasting model (PRIMA) in the Monetary Policy Report. It has a detailed supply section and is likely to produce higher inflation forecasts under a more persistent oil shock, which the BoC could use to justify a hike.

Market pricing of a hike moved from about 10bp to 20-24bp on Oct 19 and stayed there. BofA attributes the repricing to a hawkish weekend speech by Governor Macklem and the rise in inflation expectations, despite a below-expectations CPI print that day.

A BoC hike with a hawkish press conference would likely drive modest bear flattening in the GoC curve and pull forward pricing of additional hikes. Total hikes would stay around 100bp over the next year, with December moving closer to fully priced.
A surprise hold could trigger a sharp but short-lived rates rally that a hawkish press conference could reverse. BofA cites Jan 2022, when the market priced 18-20bp of a hike, as precedent.
The BoC has delivered a dovish hold only 3 times since 2008 (Dec 2017, Dec 2021, Jan 2022) in BofA's table of market pricing three days before meetings.

BofA recommends leaning long CAD rates after the BoC and fading market pricing of additional hikes, especially long Canadian rates relative to US rates. Markets price 105bp of tightening in Canada versus 67bp in the US over the next year.

BofA expects the Fed to deliver more tightening than markets price, and more than the BoC, citing stronger US data and persistently elevated US inflation. It sees CAD 2y outperforming US 2y, though the Oct BoC could be a near-term headwind.

tension_points.bull_case: Hike case: headline inflation above 3%, hawkish Macklem speech, rising inflation expectations and persistently high oil prices leave meaningful hike risk, and markets price a hike at 85%.
tension_points.bear_case: Hold case: employment fell 68.3k, unemployment is 6.5%, wage growth is 2.3% and average core inflation is 1.9%, below target, so weak activity favors a pause.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hike on Oct 28 would invalidate the hold call. A hold with a hawkish press conference that reverses the rates rally would invalidate the long CAD rates call.
